title: Lesson 32: Access and licensing rollout at scale
description: Grounded in Lesson 32 of the AI Adoption series: entitlement versus access, the eight rollout terms, per-seat, consumption and hybrid license shapes, buying below the eligible population, the identity-provider provisioning chain and its four edges, the seat funnel from purchased to habitual, and wave rollout with entry and exit gates.

questions.question: Why buy fewer seats than the number of eligible employees at the start?
options: Eligibility is a permission, and a waitlist measures who actually intends to use the tool
Buying fewer seats lowers the per-seat price that the vendor is willing to offer
Eligible employees rarely want the tool, so most of them would never log in anyway
Seat counts must almost always stay below total headcount because of standard contract terms
questions.explanation: Adoption is a behavior while eligibility is only a permission, so buying to eligibility turns a behavior question into a sunk cost and removes the waitlist that shows which teams are pulling.

questions.question: What is the most important fact about seat contracts during a rollout?
options: Price per seat falls as the total number of seats in the contract grows larger
Adding seats mid-term is easy, while removing them is a negotiation
Annual commitments always renew automatically without any notice period
Consumption pricing removes the need to track which users are active
questions.explanation: The purchased count is effectively locked until renewal, so buying ahead of demand becomes a commitment that cannot easily be reversed.

questions.question: A program reports 720 users active in the last 30 days out of 1,000 assigned and calls that 72 percent adoption. What is wrong with that figure?
options: The measurement window is too short, so the figure understates how many people truly use the tool
Assigned seats undercount real access, so the true adoption rate is higher than reported
One number hides five layers, and the habitual count predicts whether a renewal is defensible
Adoption should be measured only once a year, at the point of contract renewal
questions.explanation: Each gap between purchased, assigned, enabled, active, and habitual has a different cause, so one figure over one window cannot say whether a renewal is justified.
